t: Born in Russian-ruled Warsaw, Maria Skłodowska studied at the clandestine Flying University, then in Paris from 1891, where she married Pierre Curie in 1895 and with him announced polonium and radium in 1898.
She won the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel and the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone, the first person to win a Nobel Prize twice and the first woman to win one.
She met the barriers of her sex and her foreign birth, was vilified by the right-wing press in 1911, and died in 1934 of aplastic anaemia believed to have come from long exposure to radiation.
dyk: The Curies did not patent the process for isolating radium, and Marie Curie insisted that monetary gifts and awards go to the scientific institutions she was affiliated with rather than to her; her papers from the 1890s are still too radioactive to handle without protective clothing.
ev: Born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw, in the Russian Empire
Leaves Poland for Paris and enrols at the University of Paris to study physics, chemistry and mathematics
Announces polonium with Pierre in July and radium in December, and coins the word radioactivity
Awarded her doctorate and, in December, shares the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel
Pierre dies in a road accident; she takes his chair and becomes the first woman professor at the University of Paris
Fails by one or two votes to enter the French Academy of Sciences, and is awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
The Radium Institute is built in Paris; in the war she sets up France's first military radiology centre and mobile X-ray units
Dies of aplastic anaemia at Passy in Haute-Savoie

f.born: 7 November 1867 in Warsaw, capital of Congress Poland in the Russian Empire, as Maria Salomea Skłodowska, youngest of five children of the teachers Władysław Skłodowski and Bronisława (née Boguska)
f.died: 4 July 1934 at the Sancellemoz sanatorium in Passy, Haute-Savoie, France, aged 66, of aplastic anaemia believed to have been contracted from long-term exposure to radiation
f.role: Physicist and chemist; professor at the University of Paris from 1906, the first woman to hold such a post there; director of the Curie Laboratory in the Radium Institute, Paris (founded 1914); Nobel laureate in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911); director of the Red Cross Radiology Service in the First World War
f.known: the discovery of polonium and radium with Pierre Curie (1898); the word radioactivity; the isolation of radium; two Nobel Prizes, the first awarded to a woman; mobile X-ray units in the First World War; the Radium Institute in Paris and the Radium Institute in Warsaw
